ranking.deadlineSort: {deadline} lists jobs by the date their applications close, soonest first.

fit.body: Your fit score for the job, out of 100. When a full fit analysis isn't available yet, a quick estimate on the same scale is used. A job whose quick estimate has too little to go on is left out when you filter for Good fits and better or Great fits only. While we are still comparing quick estimates with full analyses, a job with a full analysis is placed halfway between its quick estimate and its analysed score, so its place in the list can differ from the number on its card.

practice.voice: You can answer out loud to an AI interviewer, or type your answers.

pricing.sub: Your resume, the applications board and reminders are free. A paid pass raises the daily limits on AI actions for a set number of days, and it never renews by itself.
pricing.proNote: Higher daily limits on every AI action while the pass lasts
pricing.seeAll: See every pass, pack and limit

q4.q: Where do the jobs come from?
q4.a: From public posts on employers' own hiring pages and from the source named on each job. Every job shows its source, a link to the original post and the date we last checked it. %BRAND% does not list every job on the market.

q5.a: Your resume, the applications board and reminders are free, with daily limits on AI actions. A paid pass raises those limits for a set number of days and never renews by itself. Every price and limit is on the pricing page.

q6.q: What does the fit score mean?
q6.a: It says how well your resume lines up with the job post: title and level, skills, industry, location and pay, and how your career has moved. It is not your chance of getting hired.

campus.empty: The calendar is being put together. A programme shows here once it has been checked against the employer's official page.

jobMatches.metaTitle: Jobs that fit your resume, each with its source
jobMatches.metaDescription: %BRAND% ranks open jobs by how well your resume fits. Every job leads with what's missing and names where the post came from.
jobMatches.title: Jobs ranked by fit, with the reason in plain words
jobMatches.sub: Every job gets a fit tier and leads with the gap: what the employer asks for that your resume doesn't show. Each job names its source and links to the original post.

sample.line2: They ask for SQL and Tableau. Your resume shows SQL only.
sample.line3: Source: the employer's hiring page · checked 2 days ago

s1.title: Add your resume and search
s1.body: Tell us the roles, cities and pay you want. Your resume does the rest.

s2.title: Read the gap first
s2.body: Each job shows what overlaps and what's missing before it shows a number.

s3.title: Apply on the employer's site
s3.body: Open the original post and apply there yourself. The job then moves to Applied on your board.

q1.q: Where do the jobs come from?
q1.a: From public posts on employers' own hiring pages and from the source named on each job. %BRAND% does not list every job on the market.

q2.a: By fit, freshness, what you've shown interest in and the listing source. The How ranking works page lists every factor.

resumeTailoring.metaTitle: Tailor your resume for each job
resumeTailoring.metaDescription: Make a version of your resume for one job, see every change, and confirm anything new before you download.
resumeTailoring.title: A version of your resume for each job
resumeTailoring.sub: See every change side by side. Anything the draft adds that isn't on your resume waits for you to confirm it.

sample.line1: Changed: the summary now names your data analysis projects.
sample.line2: One line has a number we couldn't find on your resume. Fix it or remove it before you download.

s1.title: Pick a job
s1.body: Start from any job in your list or one you added yourself.

s2.title: Review the changes
s2.body: Keep, edit or remove each change. Nothing new is added without your say.

s3.title: Download
s3.body: Export a PDF or Word file once every new detail is confirmed.

q1.a: It can suggest wording, but a claim, number or skill that isn't on your resume can't be downloaded until you confirm, edit or remove it.

q2.q: Does it change my main resume?
q2.a: No. Each tailored copy is separate, and your main resume stays as it is.

coverLetters.metaTitle: Cover letters from the job post and your resume
coverLetters.metaDescription: Write a cover letter for one job from the post and your own resume, then edit it.
coverLetters.title: A cover letter for this job, from your own resume
coverLetters.sub: The letter uses what the post asks for and what your resume shows. You edit it before you use it.

sample.line1: Opening names the role and the team from the post.
sample.line2: Middle paragraph uses two results from your resume.
sample.line3: Written by AI. Read it before you send it.

s2.title: Read the draft
s2.body: Every fact comes from your resume or the post.

s3.title: Edit and download
s3.body: Change anything, then copy it or download it.

q1.q: Is it sent to the employer?
q1.a: No. You decide where and whether to use it.

q2.a: Yes, a daily limit. The pricing page lists it.

readyToApply.metaTitle: Applications prepared each week; you submit them
readyToApply.metaDescription: Each week %BRAND% prepares materials for jobs that fit. You review them and submit each application yourself.
readyToApply.title: Each week, applications prepared for you to review
readyToApply.sub: For jobs that fit, %BRAND% prepares a tailored resume, a cover letter and answers to common questions. You open each application and submit it yourself.

sample.line1: 5 jobs this week · Good fit or better
sample.line2: Kit ready: tailored resume, cover letter, 4 answers
sample.line3: Open application → you check it and submit

s1.title: Set how many a week
s1.body: Choose 5, 10, 20 or 30 jobs and the lowest fit you'll accept.

s2.title: Review each kit
s2.body: Change anything before you use it.

s3.title: Submit it yourself
s3.body: Open the employer's page and submit. The job moves to Applied.

q1.a: No. It never submits an application or contacts an employer.

q2.q: What if I didn't apply after opening a job?
q2.a: Undo it in one tap and the job goes back where it was.

referralCodes.metaTitle: Referral codes shared by other job seekers
referralCodes.metaDescription: See the referral codes other %BRAND% users shared for a company. A moderator checks each one before it appears.
referralCodes.title: Referral codes for the company you're applying to
referralCodes.sub: Other %BRAND% users share the referral codes they have. A moderator checks each one before it appears, and codes that cost money are not allowed.

sample.line2: Referral code: EXAMPLE2027 · checked by a moderator
sample.line3: A code helps your application reach the company. It does not decide the outcome.

s1.title: Open a job or a company
s1.body: Codes shared for that company show on the job page and under Referral codes.

s2.title: Copy the code
s2.body: Enter it in the employer's own application form when you apply.

s3.title: Share one you have
s3.body: Add a code of your own. It appears after a moderator checks it.

q1.a: No. Codes that are sold or traded are refused, and so are codes that carry a phone number, a WeChat ID, an email or a link.

q2.q: Does a code get me the job?
q2.a: No. It helps your application reach the company. It does not decide the outcome.
